prompts.display_text: Pin a country where a new temple was dedicated in 1985 or 1986 (not rededications).
prompts.text_original: A country where a new temple was dedicated in 1985 or 1986 (not counting rededications).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (original dedication dates) and the Church temple list, read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: In 1985 Gordon B. Hinckley dedicated temples at Freiberg Germany, Stockholm Sweden, Johannesburg South Africa and Seoul Korea. In 1986 South America gained temples at Buenos Aires and Lima. Saints vol. 4 tells of Betty Campi of Argentina, who held a temple recommend while she waited for a temple in her own country.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country where a king of Assyria, Babylon or Egypt ruled or fought, in the Old Testament.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country where a king of Assyria, Babylon or Egypt ruled or fought, in the Old Testament
prompts.summary: In the later Old Testament period, Assyria, Babylon and Egypt fought over the lands around Israel. Sennacherib of Assyria besieged Lachish, Pharaoh Necho killed King Josiah at Megiddo, and Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon defeated Necho at Carchemish (Jeremiah 46:2). Nebuchadnezzar also laid a long siege to Tyre and judged King Zedekiah of Judah at Riblah in Syria (2 Kings 25:6).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Nebuchadnezzar ruled from Babylon (Daniel 4:30).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Sennacherib besieged Lachish, and Necho killed Josiah at Megiddo (2 Kings 18:14; 23:29).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Necho was king of Egypt, and Nahum recalls Assyria's sack of No-Amon, Egyptian Thebes (Nahum 3:8).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Ezekiel describes Nebuchadnezzar's long siege of Tyre (Ezekiel 26:7; 29:18).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Tiglath-pileser took Damascus, and Nebuchadnezzar judged Zedekiah at Riblah (2 Kings 16:9; 25:6).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Jeremiah's oracle against the Philistines came before Pharaoh smote Gaza (Jeremiah 47:1).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Nebuchadnezzar beat Necho at Carchemish, on the Turkish side of the border (Jeremiah 46:2; Isaiah 10:9).

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country with a place where a woman named in Acts lived.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country with a place where a woman named in Acts lived
prompts.note: Places in the West Bank or Gaza, such as Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho or Gaza city, count as Palestine, which is not an answer.
prompts.summary: Acts names several women in the early Church. Tabitha lived at Joppa, Lydia, who came from Thyatira, hosted Paul at Philippi, and Damaris believed at Athens. Priscilla and her husband Aquila had left Rome when Claudius expelled the Jews (Acts 18:2) and later lived at Ephesus.

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Lydia hosted Paul at Philippi; Damaris lived at Athens.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Tabitha lived at Joppa (Acts 9:36).

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Priscilla and Aquila had lived in Rome until Claudius expelled the Jews (Acts 18:2).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Lydia came from Thyatira; Priscilla later lived at Ephesus.

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: Queen Candace ruled Kush from Meroe (Acts 8:27).

prompts.text_original: A country where Czech, Portuguese, Tongan, Norwegian or Finnish (Book of Mormon translations 1933-1954) is an official language
prompts.summary: From 1933 to 1954 the Book of Mormon came out in Czech (1933), Portuguese (1939), Tongan (1946), Norwegian (1950) and Finnish (1954). Norwegian got its own edition a century after Danish. Portuguese opened the book to Brazil, Portugal and several African nations.

prompts.summary: Twelve Spanish-speaking countries had a dedicated temple by the end of 2000. Mexico and Chile led in 1983, followed by Guatemala, Peru and Argentina in the 1980s. The building surge of 1999 and 2000 added Spain, Colombia, Ecuador, Bolivia, the Dominican Republic, Venezuela and Costa Rica.
